name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,545

clue.text: Form of exercise is source of inflammation in Cockney's feet

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, so only its opening letter is wanted
one piece is placed inside the other, sitting within its letters

blocks.note: Cockney rhyming slang: plates of meat means feet, shortened to plates
first letter of inflammation

explanation.surface: A Cockney complains that a workout routine has left his feet sore and inflamed.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhyming slang drops the rhyming word: plates of meat for feet becomes simply plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilates is a named system of low-impact exercises for core strength, posture and flexibility.

clue.text: Performs erratically in Cambridge Footlights' productions?

blocks.note: the Footlights is Cambridge University's drama club, and what it stages are plays
a student in residence at a university such as Cambridge is said to be up

explanation.surface: A question about the student comedy shows staged by Cambridge's Footlights troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: The Footlights is the famous Cambridge student theatre and comedy club; being UP means being at university in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine or child that plays up behaves badly or malfunctions, working unreliably and unpredictably.

clue.text: Unresolved affairs soon led wayward son to consume ecstasy

indicators.note: something wayward strays from its proper course, so these letters wander out of order
consuming means taking something in, so one piece ends up inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the standard abbreviation for son
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A youngster has been led astray into drug-taking, leaving matters unsettled.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose ends are details or tasks still unfinished or unsettled after the main business is done.

clue.text: Drunken rambler crossing moor, one desperate to maintain balance

indicators.note: to cross something here is to span it from side to side, so the outer pair surrounds the inner piece

blocks.note: tight is informal for drunk
a rambler is someone who walks for pleasure
to moor a boat is to tie it up with a rope

explanation.surface: A tipsy hiker staggers over open moorland, trying not to fall over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moor' looks like the heath the rambler crosses, but it is the verb meaning to tie up a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus performer on a high wire must keep perfect equilibrium or fall, so staying upright matters desperately.

clue.text: Importance of law requiring Republican to intervene for third time

indicators.note: stepping in for the third occurrence of the abbreviation for time means taking that letter's place in the word

blocks.note: a statute is a written law
R is the abbreviation for Republican
T is the abbreviation for time; this is the letter that drops out

explanation.surface: A legal ruling needs a Republican to step in yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' is T, and STATUTE contains three; the R stands in for the third of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature means standing or reputation gained by achievement, so a figure of great stature has importance.

clue.text: That girl's suggestion sounded typical of a kid

indicators.note: sounded means spoken out, so we go by how the words are pronounced rather than spelt

blocks.note: that girl's means belonging to her
a sign is a hint or suggestion

explanation.surface: A girl's proposal was voiced in a childish way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child, but it is a young goat; the answer is a rare word, said hur-sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Hircine means goatlike, especially in smell, from Latin hircus, a he-goat; a kid is a young goat.

clue.text: Composer about to take up case of Western gunslinger

indicators.note: in a down entry, taking something up lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: Gustav Holst wrote The Planets
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A composer is about to tackle the story of a Wild West gunfighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A holster is the leather pouch worn at the hip that holds a cowboy's pistol.

clue.text: Subversive characters turn on stars

indicators.note: in a down entry, one thing on another sits above it, so the first piece comes before the second

blocks.note: a revolution is a complete turn
Aries is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: Rebellious types switch on the celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolutionaries are people working to overthrow the established political order, rebels and agitators.

clue.text: It's not appropriate to nod off during sex

indicators.note: happening during something places it within that thing, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: it is a coy word for sex
to nod off is to doze, to nap

explanation.surface: Falling asleep in the middle of lovemaking is bad form.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or ill-fitting for the occasion, the opposite of apt.

clue.text: Never-ending foreign vote is ignored

indicators.note: something ignored is left out, so those letters are dropped from the word

blocks.note: external means from outside, foreign
a voter marks the ballot with a cross, X

explanation.surface: Votes cast abroad keep getting overlooked, endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means lasting forever, without beginning or end, so it has no conclusion.

clue.text: In the middle of day, arrested by American Government

indicators.note: someone arrested is held by captors, so these letters are held inside the others

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
G is the abbreviation for government
Mon is the abbreviation for Monday

explanation.surface: Someone was detained by US authorities partway through the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Among means surrounded by or in the midst of a group of things or people.

clue.text: Make light of everyone having wandered naked

indicators.note: naked means stripped of covering, so the outer letters are removed

blocks.note: everyone means all
to wander off course is to deviate

explanation.surface: Everyone made fun of the streaker who went running about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make light of' looks like a single phrase meaning to joke about; the definition is only 'Make light', in the sense of lightening a load.
explanation.definitionFit: To alleviate a burden or pain is to ease it, making it lighter or less severe to bear.

clue.text: Leisurewear, its use at work initially is relaxed

indicators.note: initially points to the start, so only the opening letter is kept
something relaxed has loosened its rigid order, so these letters are free to rearrange

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of work

explanation.surface: Casual clothing is now acceptable in the office as dress codes loosen.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracksuit-style outfit of loose top and trousers is worn for lounging or exercise, casual clothing.

clue.text: Oddly picked least popular school subject

indicators.note: picking oddly means taking only the letters in odd positions, first, third and fifth

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters of least
something popular is in fashion, in

explanation.surface: Pupils oddly chose the subject nobody likes.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin, the language of ancient Rome, is a traditional classroom subject in many schools.

clue.text: Small cavity features on putting green

blocks.note: a putting green has a pin, the flagstick, and a hole

explanation.surface: A little dip is one of the features of a golf putting green.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'features' asks for two things found on a green, the pin and the hole, placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinhole is a tiny hole such as a pin would make, a very small opening or gap.

clue.text: Hearing once again Blair term essentially needs reviewing

indicators.note: the essence lies inside, so the letters wanted sit within the phrase rather than at its edges
to review is literally to view again from the other direction, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters inside the phrase, with its first and last letters left aside

explanation.surface: A look back at Tony Blair's time in office calls for fresh scrutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needs reviewing' looks like an anagram signal, but the letters simply run backwards inside the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A retrial is a second trial of the same case, so the court hears it a further time.

clue.text: Heading of mother's recipe is wildly inaccurate

indicators.note: the heading is what comes at the top, so only the first letter is taken
acting wildly means out of control, so these letters scatter into a new order

blocks.note: first letter of mother
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mum's cooking instructions are way off the mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprecise means lacking exactness, vague and loose, so it is not accurate.

clue.text: Postpone broadcast covering product's differentiating factor

indicators.note: a cover goes round the outside, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: to broadcast a signal is to send it out
USP is a unique selling point, what makes a product stand out

explanation.surface: A marketing team delays airing an advert about what makes their product special.
explanation.walkthrough: USP, unique selling point, is a marketing term for a product's distinctive advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to halt it temporarily or put it off until later, delaying it.

clue.text: Struggle with overcooked starter instead of cold dish

indicators.note: putting one thing instead of another swaps them, so one letter takes another's place
a starter is what comes first, so only the opening letter of the word before it is used

blocks.note: a scuffle is a brief struggle
first letter of overcooked
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A cook battles with a starter that went too long, serving a cold dish in its place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold dish' looks like the definition, but cold is the letter being replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: A soufflé is a light baked or chilled preparation of eggs whipped with other ingredients, served as a course.

clue.text: Extremely disconsolate graduate, regularly called a failure

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the first and last letters are kept
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: first and last letters of disconsolate
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
first, third and fifth letters of called

explanation.surface: A graduate, utterly downcast, is often labelled a flop.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden humiliating collapse or fiasco, a total disaster of an outcome.

clue.text: Do well in brief Shakespearean role

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: Prospero is the magician in The Tempest

explanation.surface: An actor shines in a short Shakespeare part.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to thrive or flourish, succeeding especially in material terms.

clue.text: Artist is well following unnatural dietary cravings

indicators.note: coming after something means being placed behind it, so this piece goes second

blocks.note: pica is the medical name for craving non-food substances such as chalk
is shortened to 's, as in it's
so and well are both used to open a remark

explanation.surface: A painter is healthy again after a spell of strange food cravings.
explanation.walkthrough: PICA is an eating disorder involving cravings for things that are not food.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso, the Spanish co-founder of Cubism, is among the most famous painters of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Gags despicable individuals told

indicators.note: told means spoken, so the word is judged by how it is said

blocks.note: wretches are contemptible people; the silent W makes them sound identical

explanation.surface: Jokes told by nasty people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gags' wants to be jokes, as the surface suggests, but here it is the verb for heaving.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is to choke or heave as if about to vomit, which is what someone who retches does.

clue.text: Extreme overhaul transforms houses

indicators.note: to house something is to hold it inside, so the letters sit within the phrase

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A radical refurbishment completely changes people's homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultra is used as an adjective for going beyond the usual, as in ultra views, radical or fanatical.

clue.text: Step in tango right to attract judge's close notice

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter is used
attracting draws the next pieces along behind, so they are added in sequence

blocks.note: T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet
R is the abbreviation for right
last letter of judge
an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A dance move in the tango is designed to catch the judges' eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A tread is a single footstep or the sound of one, a step taken in walking.

clue.text: Group disheartened by a holiday in foreign capital

indicators.note: losing heart means losing the centre, so the middle letter is removed

blocks.note: a bunch is a group
taken as written
a holiday is a rest

explanation.surface: A group of travellers feels down after a trip to an overseas city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucharest is the capital city of Romania, a capital outside Britain.

clue.text: Gratuitous thrills? Footballers attempt to defend them

blocks.note: gratuitous can mean given without charge
kicks are thrills, as in doing something for kicks

explanation.surface: Pointless excitement, then a scene of players lining up to block a shot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the answer by what happens to it: defenders form a wall to block free kicks.
explanation.definitionFit: Free kicks are set pieces awarded after fouls, which the defending side tries to block with a wall.

clue.text: Independent rule is hard for certain type of setter

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for independent
R is an abbreviation for rule
taken as written
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Self-rule is difficult for one kind of crossword compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler, but it is the dog: the Irish setter is a red gundog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish setter is a recognised breed of red-coated gundog, one particular kind among the setter breeds.

clue.text: Support Red Nose activity

indicators.note: activity means busy motion, so these letters are stirred into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Back a charity fundraising event.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Nose Day is a British charity telethon where people wear red clown noses to raise money.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a cause or candidate is to give it public approval and backing.

clue.text: Every other Tory is at new restaurant's opening, having southern shellfish

indicators.note: every other means skipping alternately, so only the second, fourth and so on are kept
an opening is where something begins, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters of the phrase
first letter of restaurant
S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: Conservatives at a newly opened restaurant all order seafood from the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Oysters are bivalve molluscs eaten raw or cooked, a classic kind of seafood.
